Bind the Gate 1 live-evidence profile's provider pin and spend ceiling to the offline manifest, and give the surface its first static guard.

FINDING (new, not from the PR #44 review). assertLiveEvidenceProfileMatchesManifest (packages/core/src/live-evidence-profile.ts:390-491) compares the manifest digest, benchmarkId, benchmarkRevision, the case-id bijection, each case's owner/repository/baseBranch, and identity distinctness. It never compares the provider pin or the budgets, and decodeBudgets (:227-239) accepts any finite non-negative maxSpendUsd. All three committed manifest cases declare modelAdapter {provider: ollama, paid: false, inputUsdPerMillionTokens: 0, outputUsdPerMillionTokens: 0} and budgets.maxCostUsd: 0. So a profile carrying the exact reviewed manifest digest, correct repository identities and a self-consistent digest-bound approval can legally pin a paid remote model at an arbitrary spend ceiling. Third instance on this surface of the same defect class: bind the fields that are easy to compare, miss the field that decides blast radius.

SCOPE
1. Bind profile.budgets.maxSpendUsd <= the manifest cases' budgets.maxCostUsd.
2. Refuse a paid provider pin when the manifest declares modelAdapter.paid === false (profile provider rates must be zero or null).
3. Bind profile.provider.kind to the manifest's modelAdapter.provider.
4. Deliberately NOT bound, each with a recorded reason in ADR 0050: model (the manifest names the FIXTURE model icarus-gate1-fixture-model-v1 — binding it would make a live run impossible), adapterVersion, transport, expectedRequests, credentials. These describe the offline replay; a live run legitimately differs. Not-binding must be a decision here, not an omission — that is the lesson of this surface.
5. Fold in the S0 debt: live-evidence is the ONLY authority surface in the repo with no assertion in scripts/security-check.mjs (30+ named assertions, zero for live-evidence) and no file under tests/security/. Add both.
6. Add a digest-projection guard: liveEvidenceProfileApprovalDigest (:299-327) hand-lists 9 fields and is complete today, but a field added later would be silently unsigned. Drive a test off the decoded record's keys.

DO NOT add the ADR 0045 row to docs/DECISIONS.md — codex's unpushed branch already adds rows for 0044-0048 including 0045. Write race, not a free fix.

The Gate 1 live-evidence manifest binding is caller-asserted. It authenticates nothing.

`packages/core/src/live-evidence-profile.ts:417`

    if (profile.offlineManifestDigest !== digest(manifestDigest, "manifestDigest")) {

`assertLiveEvidenceProfileMatchesManifest(profile, manifest, manifestDigest)` receives the parsed manifest OBJECT and its digest STRING as two independent caller-supplied arguments and never links them: it compares the profile's pin to the caller's parameter. `digestJson` is imported at :1 but used only for the approval digest at :344. The digest of `manifest` is never computed.

Consequence: every binding ADR 0045 and ADR 0050 added — repository identity, provider kind, unpaid-means-unpaid, spend ceiling — is evaluated against whatever manifest object the caller passes, while the digest check passes on the reviewed manifest's digest string. ADR 0045 property 1 states "Changing the manifest invalidates the profile." That is false.

DEMONSTRATED (three independent reproductions: a hunt agent, a skeptic tasked with refuting it, and by hand):

    refused   CONTROL: paid anthropic @ $500 vs the REVIEWED manifest
                -> profile pins provider anthropic, but offline manifest case
                   typescript-library-repair pins ollama
    sha256(reviewed bytes) = 692bbfe17ba1b998...
    sha256(edited bytes)   = 3b78aefc89f91238...
    ADMITTED  EDITED manifest (anthropic/paid/$500, owner=attacker) + the REVIEWED digest string

NOT exploitable today: `authorizeLiveEvidenceRun` has no production caller (only the index.ts:160 barrel export and tests). That is precisely why it is filed now — the case executor is the next slice, and building it against this signature bakes in a decorative binding.

FIX SHAPE (not implemented; needs its own ADR): take the manifest BYTES rather than a parsed object plus a digest, compute the digest inside the function, and parse from the same bytes that were hashed.

ALSO FOUND, same surface, not fixed:
- HIGH: an `ollama` pin is assumed loopback (no credential, nothing charged) but `decodeProvider` (:216-228) validates baseUrl shape only and never calls `parseProviderBaseUrl`, which computes locality. `{kind:"ollama", baseUrl:"https://exfil.invalid/"}` is admitted. This lands on Kevin's decision to pin loopback Ollama so the zero ceilings are honest — nothing enforces it.
- MEDIUM: `maxRuntimeSeconds` is bounded by nothing. `decodeBudgets` (:245-256) accepts any positive integer; the manifest loop binds `maxCostUsd` but never the sibling `maxActiveRuntimeMs` pinned at 1,200,000 ms/case. ADR 0050 bound money and skipped wall clock.

REFUTED, do not re-raise without new evidence: landing `credentialRef.name` not allowlist-checked (the coordinator refuses before its first effect); `derivativeEffects.disposition` self-asserted (gates nothing at runtime).

Independent review of the Gate 1 live-evidence slice that shipped without one. `docs/evals/2026-08-23-gate1-live-3of3.md` records "The operator explicitly overrode the otherwise-required independent review for this slice", so commits b250eb0, 6b4f8f0 and b62a929 (~5,700 lines) reached main unreviewed. This is the one confirmed defect.

## The defect

`b62a929` — the commit that RECORDS the 3/3 evidence — also relaxes a security invariant in `packages/github-gateway/src/gateway.ts`. `#readPullRequest` previously required `maintainer_can_modify` to be a boolean, always. It now accepts `null`/`undefined` and coerces to `false` when a new `listedSameRepositoryHead` parameter is true, which `readPullRequestByHead` passes unconditionally.

**Nothing verifies that the head is in the same repository.** The listing is filtered by `head: <owner>:<branch>`, which GitHub scopes by head USER, not head REPOSITORY, and the two invariants that follow only compare `head.ref` (branch name, `readHeadBranch`, gateway.ts:829-839) and `base.ref`. No code reads `head.repo`. So the parameter names a property the code never establishes.

The stated justification is also mis-attributed: GitHub omits `maintainer_can_modify` because the LIST endpoint returns a *simple* pull-request object, not because the head is same-repository. The omission is therefore universal on this path, not conditional on the property the flag claims.

## Why it matters

`maintainerCanModify` is pinned as the LITERAL `false` in the digest-bound landing record — `landing-records.ts:214, 1558, 2906`, validated by `literal(...)` at `:1328, :1839, :2158, :2391`. The create path must still PROVE that value (correctly kept, and tested). The reconcile path may now SYNTHESIZE it. A reconciled landing receipt can assert an observation that was never made, in a field the record treats as a pinned security property — and reconciliation is exactly the crash-recovery path, where receipt honesty matters most.

Fails-closed note, in fairness: a genuine `true` from GitHub is a boolean, so it survives the coercion and is then rejected by `literal(..., false)`. Only the absent/null case synthesizes.

## The test cannot fail

`tests/provider/github-gateway.test.ts` — "normalizes GitHub'"'"'s omitted maintainer flag when listing a same-repository head" asserts the name but not the property: `pullRequestEntry` builds `head: { ref, sha }` with NO `repo` member (test file :35), so the fixture cannot express same-repository vs fork. The test passes identically either way.

## Proven, not asserted

A read-only probe (`scratchpad/icarus-crossrepo-probe.test.ts`) lists a PR whose head is `attacker/icarus-fork` with `maintainer_can_modify` omitted. `readPullRequestByHead` returns `{ number: 42, maintainerCanModify: false }` — the relaxation fires for a cross-repository head. Probe passes on `b62a929`.

## Exploitability — honest bound

Not exploitable in Gate 1'"'"'s own use: Icarus creates `icarus/<run-id>` heads in the target repo via absent-only ref creation, so its own heads are same-repository. Reaching it needs a same-owner fork carrying a branch whose name matches an unguessed run-id UUID. This is a record-integrity defect, the same class and severity as ADR 0053'"'"'s provider-host finding (downgraded because no consumer had it yet), not a live vulnerability.

## Suggested remediation (proposal only — not implemented)

Read `head.repo.full_name` and compare it to `${owner}/${repository}`; pass the relaxation only when they match, and refuse when `head.repo` is absent. Then make the test express both heads so it can fail. This is security-sensitive code and takes the PR path plus a non-author seat per the repo contract.

Independent review of the Gate 1 live-evidence slice that shipped without one. `docs/evals/2026-08-23-gate1-live-3of3.md` records "The operator explicitly overrode the otherwise-required independent review for this slice", so commits b250eb0, 6b4f8f0 and b62a929 (~5,700 lines) reached main unreviewed. This is the one confirmed defect.

## The defect

`b62a929` — the commit that RECORDS the 3/3 evidence — also relaxes a security invariant in `packages/github-gateway/src/gateway.ts`. `#readPullRequest` previously required `maintainer_can_modify` to be a boolean, always. It now accepts `null`/`undefined` and coerces to `false` when a new `listedSameRepositoryHead` parameter is true, which `readPullRequestByHead` passes unconditionally.

**Nothing verifies that the head is in the same repository.** The listing is filtered by `head: <owner>:<branch>`, which GitHub scopes by head USER, not head REPOSITORY, and the two invariants that follow only compare `head.ref` (branch name, `readHeadBranch`, gateway.ts:829-839) and `base.ref`. No code reads `head.repo`. So the parameter names a property the code never establishes.

The stated justification is also mis-attributed: GitHub omits `maintainer_can_modify` because the LIST endpoint returns a *simple* pull-request object, not because the head is same-repository. The omission is therefore universal on this path, not conditional on the property the flag claims.

## Why it matters

`maintainerCanModify` is pinned as the LITERAL `false` in the digest-bound landing record — `landing-records.ts:214, 1558, 2906`, validated by `literal(...)` at `:1328, :1839, :2158, :2391`. The create path must still PROVE that value (correctly kept, and tested). The reconcile path may now SYNTHESIZE it. A reconciled landing receipt can assert an observation that was never made, in a field the record treats as a pinned security property — and reconciliation is exactly the crash-recovery path, where receipt honesty matters most.

Fails-closed note, in fairness: a genuine `true` from GitHub is a boolean, so it survives the coercion and is then rejected by `literal(..., false)`. Only the absent/null case synthesizes.

## The test cannot fail

`tests/provider/github-gateway.test.ts` — "normalizes GitHub'"'"'s omitted maintainer flag when listing a same-repository head" asserts the name but not the property: `pullRequestEntry` builds `head: { ref, sha }` with NO `repo` member (test file :35), so the fixture cannot express same-repository vs fork. The test passes identically either way.

## Proven, not asserted

A read-only probe (`scratchpad/icarus-crossrepo-probe.test.ts`) lists a PR whose head is `attacker/icarus-fork` with `maintainer_can_modify` omitted. `readPullRequestByHead` returns `{ number: 42, maintainerCanModify: false }` — the relaxation fires for a cross-repository head. Probe passes on `b62a929`.

## Exploitability — honest bound

Not exploitable in Gate 1'"'"'s own use: Icarus creates `icarus/<run-id>` heads in the target repo via absent-only ref creation, so its own heads are same-repository. Reaching it needs a same-owner fork carrying a branch whose name matches an unguessed run-id UUID. This is a record-integrity defect, the same class and severity as ADR 0053'"'"'s provider-host finding (downgraded because no consumer had it yet), not a live vulnerability.

## Suggested remediation (proposal only — not implemented)

Read `head.repo.full_name` and compare it to `${owner}/${repository}`; pass the relaxation only when they match, and refuse when `head.repo` is absent. Then make the test express both heads so it can fail. This is security-sensitive code and takes the PR path plus a non-author seat per the repo contract.

## Acceptance
